reviewQuestions: Are GPAI and systemic-risk applicability tests defensible?
Are transparency and copyright obligations represented?
Are provider-specific external obligations clearly bounded?
scope: GPAI provider role and open-source exceptions
Articles 53 to 55 documentation, downstream information and copyright controls
model-level evidence and external evaluation boundaries
officialSources: European Commission GPAI guidance and Code of Practice where legally relevant

preReviewFindings.finding: The platform cannot determine that a customer is a GPAI provider or that a model has systemic risk solely from questionnaire answers.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Approve applicability logic and mandatory evidence/escalation conditions.

preReviewFindings.finding: Copyright policy, training-content summary and downstream technical information depend on model-provider evidence.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Define minimum evidence and permissible product claims.

preReviewFindings.finding: External evaluation, adversarial testing, incident reporting and cybersecurity duties cannot be proven by repository tests.
preReviewFindings.requiredDecision: Confirm external specialist and operational evidence requirements.

acceptanceCriteria: GPAI role and systemic-risk tests are cautious and evidence-based.
Open-source exceptions are not applied automatically.
Copyright, transparency and downstream-information duties are represented without overclaiming.
Model-level external obligations remain explicit customer/provider responsibilities.
limitations: The platform does not inspect model weights, training corpora or compute by itself.
Systemic-risk designation and technical adequacy require external evidence.
Questionnaire completion is not proof of GPAI compliance.
